purpose: Test the concrete local-to-finite mismatch by fitting actual native deletion fractions against finite source effects; compare same-context Euclidean, Fisher and one-scale controls; measure an untrained future-position endpoint.
scope: Retained exposed natural development, same 24 source-only anchors and Euclidean-coarsened source gates, same target128 pools, one controlled seed edge and two mechanisms. Pointwise Fisher uses model-distribution score samples on discovery; source and target gates are native nonnegative deletion fractions. Same-row Euclidean, pointwise, shuffled-response and amplitude controls receive identical source operation and target pool. Actual model ablations on calibration remain development, with next-token response secondary and not independent causal semantics. No new dataset, seed, or main-conference claim. Adaptive finite follow-up after observing mixed v1 results. Frozen source groups, target pools and retained discovery gradients reused. A source-balanced96-entry discovery design refits all new methods. Actual gate and one-scale KL fits share initialization, minibatches,64updates and learning rate; all old methods remain. Offset4 future-token distribution is not an objective or selector input, measured only after fitting. This is an additional functional endpoint, not proof of semantic identity or an independent model.
